request.text:
You are the vision observer for GeoKnow / ESOGU "foraminifera-fossil".
You are NOT a taxonomic authority and you do NOT replace the project's scoring engine.

Goal: look at the attached optical image(s) of a microfossil (thin section or reflected-light photomicrograph) and fill the project's character sheet CHR_01–CHR_21.

Hard rules
1. Observe first. Identify only as a tentative suggestion.
2. Never invent a character. If it is not clearly visible, use state NOT_OBSERVABLE. If visible but ambiguous, use UNCERTAIN.
3. NOT_OBSERVABLE is not ABSENT. Do not mark ABSENT unless the relevant area is exposed and the feature is clearly missing.
4. Keep CHR_05 and CHR_06 separate:
   - CHR_05 = serial arrangement only (UNISERIAL, BISERIAL, TRISERIAL, QUINQUELOCULINE, TRILOCULINE, BILOCULINE, ANNULAR, CYCLIC, IRREGULAR_SERIAL, OTHER)
   - CHR_06 = coiling (PLANISPIRAL, TROCHOSPIRAL, STREPTOSPIRAL, GLOMOSPIRAL, IRREGULAR_COILING, UNCOILED)
5. Do not force a species name. Prefer genus or morphogroup. If evidence is weak, identification_status = INDETERMINATE.
6. This tool is academic and non-commercial. Do not present the answer as an official Foraminifera.eu, WoRMS, or museum determination.
7. Reply with VALID JSON only. No markdown, no preamble, no trailing text.
8. Allowed observation states: PRESENT, ABSENT, NOT_OBSERVABLE, UNCERTAIN.
9. Allowed identification_status values: CONFIRMED_GENUS, PROBABLE_GENUS, CANDIDATE_GENUS, INDETERMINATE, NO_MATCH_WITHIN_CORE_TAXA.
10. If the object is not a foraminifer, set object_is_foraminifer=false and fill every CHR with NOT_OBSERVABLE / null.

Allowed values (use ONLY these codes)

CHR_01 Test composition: AGGLUTINATED | PORCELANEOUS | HYALINE | UNCERTAIN
CHR_02 Test shape: GLOBULAR | SAC_LIKE | TUBULAR | ELONGATE | FUSIFORM | OVOID | LENTICULAR | DISCOIDAL | FLATTENED | CONICAL | HIGH_CONICAL | FLABELLIFORM | STELLATE | IRREGULAR | OTHER | NOT_OBSERVABLE | UNCERTAIN
CHR_03 Septation: PRESENT | ABSENT | NOT_OBSERVABLE | UNCERTAIN
CHR_04 Chamber number organization: UNDIVIDED | MULTICHAMBERED | NOT_OBSERVABLE | UNCERTAIN
CHR_05 Chamber arrangement: UNISERIAL | BISERIAL | TRISERIAL | QUINQUELOCULINE | TRILOCULINE | BILOCULINE | ANNULAR | CYCLIC | IRREGULAR_SERIAL | OTHER | NOT_OBSERVABLE | UNCERTAIN
CHR_06 Coiling pattern: PLANISPIRAL | TROCHOSPIRAL | STREPTOSPIRAL | GLOMOSPIRAL | IRREGULAR_COILING | UNCOILED | NOT_OBSERVABLE | UNCERTAIN
CHR_07 Coiling plane: SINGLE_PLANE | CHANGING_PLANES | MULTIDIRECTIONAL | NOT_APPLICABLE | NOT_OBSERVABLE | UNCERTAIN
CHR_08 Involution/evolution: INVOLUTE | SEMI_INVOLUTE | EVOLUTE | NOT_APPLICABLE | NOT_OBSERVABLE | UNCERTAIN
CHR_09 Ontogenetic arrangement change: NONE | PLANISPIRAL_TO_UNISERIAL | PLANISPIRAL_TO_BISERIAL | BISERIAL_TO_UNISERIAL | TRISERIAL_TO_BISERIAL | TRISERIAL_TO_UNISERIAL | COILED_TO_SERIAL | OTHER | NOT_OBSERVABLE | UNCERTAIN
CHR_10 Internal complexity: SIMPLE | SUBDIVIDED | COMPLEX | RETICULATE | LABYRINTHIC | NOT_OBSERVABLE | UNCERTAIN
CHR_11 Secondary chamberlets: PRESENT | ABSENT | WEAKLY_DEVELOPED | WELL_DEVELOPED | NOT_OBSERVABLE | UNCERTAIN
CHR_12 Embryonic apparatus: SIMPLE | BILOCULAR | MULTILOCULAR | COMPLEX | NOT_OBSERVABLE | UNCERTAIN
CHR_13 Radial/internal partitions: ABSENT | RADIAL | VERTICAL | SUBEPIDERMAL | RETICULATE | OTHER | NOT_OBSERVABLE | UNCERTAIN
CHR_14 Pillars: PRESENT | ABSENT | WEAK | STRONG | NOT_OBSERVABLE | UNCERTAIN
CHR_15 Lateral chamberlets: PRESENT | ABSENT | WEAKLY_DEVELOPED | WELL_DEVELOPED | NOT_OBSERVABLE | UNCERTAIN
CHR_16 Aperture type: TERMINAL | INTERIOMARGINAL | BASAL | MULTIPLE | SLIT_LIKE | CRIBRATE | OTHER | NOT_OBSERVABLE | UNCERTAIN
CHR_17 Marginal cord: PRESENT | ABSENT | WEAK | STRONG | NOT_OBSERVABLE | UNCERTAIN
CHR_18 Septal filaments: ABSENT | SIMPLE | CURVED | WAVY | RETICULATE | COMPLEX | NOT_OBSERVABLE | UNCERTAIN
CHR_19 Attachment mode: FREE | ATTACHED | NOT_OBSERVABLE | UNCERTAIN
CHR_20 Dimorphism: PRESENT | ABSENT | MEGALOSPHERIC_FORM | MICROSPHERIC_FORM | NOT_OBSERVABLE | UNCERTAIN
CHR_21 Section orientation: AXIAL | EQUATORIAL | OBLIQUE | TANGENTIAL | UNKNOWN

Observation object format for every CHR:
{"value": "<CODE or null>", "state": "PRESENT|ABSENT|NOT_OBSERVABLE|UNCERTAIN", "reason": "one short sentence"}

When state is NOT_OBSERVABLE or UNCERTAIN, value may be null.
For CHR_01, if composition cannot be judged from lighting, value=UNCERTAIN and state=UNCERTAIN.
For CHR_21, state is usually PRESENT and value is the section type; use UNKNOWN if the view is external, not a thin section.

Context from the user:
- locality: unknown
- age / stratigraphy: unknown
- lighting / magnification: unknown
- scale: unknown
- views provided: unknown

{
  "object_is_foraminifer": true,
  "image_quality": "good",
  "image_type": "thin_section",
  "observations": {
    "CHR_01": {"value": "PORCELANEOUS", "state": "PRESENT", "reason": "The microgranular to porcelaneous wall structure is typical of porcelaneous larger foraminifers."},
    "CHR_02": {"value": "OVOID", "state": "PRESENT", "reason": "The overall shape of the test in this section is ovoid to elongate."},
    "CHR_03": {"value": "PRESENT", "state": "PRESENT", "reason": "Septa separating chambers are clearly visible."},
    "CHR_04": {"value": "MULTICHAMBERED", "state": "PRESENT", "reason": "Many chambers are arranged in whorls."},
    "CHR_05": {"value": "NOT_OBSERVABLE", "state": "NOT_OBSERVABLE", "reason": "Serial arrangement is not applicable for this coiled form."},
    "CHR_06": {"value": "STREPTOSPIRAL", "state": "PRESENT", "reason": "The early coils show an axis change indicative of streptospiral coiling."},
    "CHR_07": {"value": "CHANGING_PLANES", "state": "PRESENT", "reason": "Coiling axis shifts during ontogeny."},
    "CHR_08": {"value": "INVOLUTE", "state": "PRESENT", "reason": "Later whorls embrace and cover earlier ones completely."},
    "CHR_09": {"value": "NONE", "state": "PRESENT", "reason": "No major stage change in coiling mode during ontogeny."},
    "CHR_10": {"value": "COMPLEX", "state": "PRESENT", "reason": "Internal structure features complex subdivisions and chamberlets."},
    "CHR_11": {"value": "WELL_DEVELOPED", "state": "PRESENT", "reason": "Secondary chamberlets and partitions are clearly visible within the wall/chambers."},
    "CHR_12": {"value": "SIMPLE", "state": "PRESENT", "reason": "Initial chamber is rounded and distinct."},
    "CHR_13": {"value": "SUBEPIDERMAL", "state": "PRESENT", "reason": "Subepidermal partitions or a network are clearly visible beneath the outer wall."},
    "CHR_14": {"value": "ABSENT", "state": "ABSENT", "reason": "Pillars are not a prominent feature in this section."},
    "CHR_15": {"value": "WELL_DEVELOPED", "state": "PRESENT", "reason": "Lateral chamberlets are developed across the wall."},
    "CHR_16": {"value": "MULTIPLE", "state": "PRESENT", "reason": "Multiple apertures or pores are visible along the face in advanced sections."},
    "CHR_17": {"value": "ABSENT", "state": "ABSENT", "reason": "No marginal cord is present."},
    "CHR_18": {"value": "ABSENT", "state": "ABSENT", "reason": "Septal filaments are not visible in this internal thin section."},
    "CHR_19": {"value": "FREE", "state": "PRESENT", "reason": "Test is free-living."},
    "CHR_20": {"value": "NOT_OBSERVABLE", "state": "NOT_OBSERVABLE", "reason": "Dimorphism cannot be determined from this single random section."},
    "CHR_21": {"value": "AXIAL", "state": "PRESENT", "reason": "The section cuts through the coiling axis showing shifting whorls."}
  },
  "module": "PORCELANEOUS",
  "vlm_suggestion": {
    "identification_status": "PROBABLE_GENUS",
    "best_open_id": "Raskovskya or Pseudedomia group",
    "candidate_genera": [{"name": "Pseudedomia", "confidence": "moderate", "why": "Complex internal chamberlets and streptospiral to flabelliform ontogeny."}],
    "lookalikes": ["Murgella", "Praeradiolites"],
    "why_not_species_level": "Section orientation and specific internal measurements are needed for species determination."
  },
  "student_explanation_en": "This is an axial thin section of a complex porcelaneous larger foraminifer. It displays streptospiral to flabelliform coiling and well-developed subepidermal partitions, characteristic of Late Cretaceous complex benthic foraminifers.",
  "student_explanation_tr": "Bu örnek, karmaşık bir kavuk yapısına ve streptospiral-flabelliform kıvrılma gösteren porselenimsi duvar yapısına sahip iri bentik foraminiferin eksenel kesitidir. Alt kretase/üst kretase formlarını anımsatır.",
  "expert_checklist_tr": [
    "Eksenel kesitin doğruluğu kontrol edildi mi?",
    "Duvar yapısının porselenimsi karakteri net mi?",
    "Subepidermal bölmelerin varlığı teyit edildi mi?"
  ],
  "disclaimer_tr": "Bu bir öğretim ve karar-destek çıktısıdır; resmi taksonomik teşhis değildir."
}

CHR_01.reason: The microgranular to porcelaneous wall structure is typical of porcelaneous larger foraminifers.

CHR_02.reason: The overall shape of the test in this section is ovoid to elongate.

CHR_03.reason: Septa separating chambers are clearly visible.

CHR_04.reason: Many chambers are arranged in whorls.

CHR_05.reason: Serial arrangement is not applicable for this coiled form.

CHR_06.reason: The early coils show an axis change indicative of streptospiral coiling.

CHR_08.reason: Later whorls embrace and cover earlier ones completely.

CHR_09.reason: No major stage change in coiling mode during ontogeny.

CHR_10.reason: Internal structure features complex subdivisions and chamberlets.

CHR_11.reason: Secondary chamberlets and partitions are clearly visible within the wall/chambers.

CHR_12.reason: Initial chamber is rounded and distinct.

CHR_13.reason: Subepidermal partitions or a network are clearly visible beneath the outer wall.

CHR_14.reason: Pillars are not a prominent feature in this section.

CHR_15.reason: Lateral chamberlets are developed across the wall.

CHR_16.reason: Multiple apertures or pores are visible along the face in advanced sections.

CHR_18.reason: Septal filaments are not visible in this internal thin section.

CHR_20.reason: Dimorphism cannot be determined from this single random section.

CHR_21.reason: The section cuts through the coiling axis showing shifting whorls.

candidate_genera.name: Pseudedomia
candidate_genera.why: Complex internal chamberlets and streptospiral to flabelliform ontogeny.
